Shouldn't that be ws_debug?

Now it shows up all the time, even when opening other formats, like BLF.
Yea, I'll fix that.  I was focused on the condition itself and the "former" debug level it was at (which seems bad if you're trying to open a k12 file) thinking it was isolated to that filetype.

> I was focused on the condition itself and the "former" debug level it was at (which seems bad if you're trying to open a k12 file) thinking it was isolated to that filetype.

The file open process is done by trying multiple file types, in order, until one of them returns "this is one of my files". There's no external metadata to indicate the file type (file extensions are a *hint*, but, especially for file types from UN\*X command-line tools, there's no *guarantee* that the file has an extension at all, so we can't use them).

So, until the opener has determined that the file is a file of its type, no "file is too short" or "the data I read isn't what I'm expecting" error is a bad thing, it's just an indication that the file *isn't* of its type, and it should return "not my file type" and let other file openers, possibly including the opener for the file whose type it is (if we have one), try it.
ws_debug would make more sense, so it does not show up that often!?
